social.hook: First of four — and I wouldn't be back for nine years.
social.caption: Joe Jackson played 20 songs that night in Anaheim. I filed it away and didn't return until 2012, which tells you something about how I make plans.
beats: August 2003. The year I also saw Peter Gabriel, The Human League, and The Cure.
Joe Jackson played 20 songs. A full set, nothing held back.
I didn't know it was the first of four. You never do, the first time.
Nine years before I saw him again. Some gaps you don't notice until you count them.

social.hook: Four times in 25 years — and only once did they not have top billing.
social.caption: That one exception was 1991, opening for Siouxsie and the Banshees. August 2016 at Birchmere was the headlining version, and it's the last time I've seen them.
beats: I saw The Smithereens four times across 25 years. Three were headline sets.
The odd one out was December 1991 — they opened for Siouxsie and the Banshees.
August 2016 at Birchmere was the headliner version. Also my only show there ever.
It's the most recent time I've seen them. Ten years ago today.

social.hook: The English Beat opened — and I'd end up seeing them 9 more times after that night.
social.caption: The Human League were the headliner, but The English Beat were the surprise that stuck. I was back to see them again less than a month later.
beats: The English Beat opened. I'd seen them before, but this night started a run — 9 more shows after this one.
The Human League played 17 songs. I wouldn't see them again for 15 years.
2003 was a dense year: Peter Gabriel, Joe Jackson, The Cure. This night was in the middle of all of it.
The English Beat were back at another venue on September 20th — 27 days later. I was there for that one too.

social.hook: They closed on 'Love Will Tear Us Apart' — and I didn't find my way back for 37 years.
social.caption: New Order in 1985, with A Certain Ratio opening — two acts I'd never see together again, and one I'd never see at all after that night. The second New Order show didn't happen until 2022.
beats: A Certain Ratio opened. I haven't seen them since — that night is the only one.
New Order closed a 14-song set with 'Love Will Tear Us Apart'. Joy Division's song, their encore.
1985 was a crowded year: Springsteen, Depeche Mode, Tears For Fears. This was the show I didn't follow up.
37 years passed before I bought another New Order ticket. The 1985 version of me had no idea.
